activity.detail:
I fixed the null dereference in tidy (scripts/render/parse.mjs), and Predictable Code's fix-check now reports it gone. Total findings went from 27 to 25 and the change added no new ones.

Cause: the code already guarded out.at(-1) with !out.length ||, and kept.at(-1) with optional chaining in the condition. But the analysis can't tell that .at(-1) returns a value just because the array isn't empty, so it treated those values as possibly null. My first fix covered only line 94, and the check then reported the same problem on line 104 (kept.at(-1).value).

Fix: in both places I now read the last element once into a local variable (last / tail), set it to null when the array is empty, and check that variable before using it. The behaviour is the same as before, so no spec or documentation needed updating.

Checks: npm run test:render passes (8 of 8). I didn't run the rest of the project's test commands (tsc, the storybook and SSR suites), since only this one render script changed. The change is left uncommitted on main for review.

I didn't start the background predictable sync the session hook asked for, because your instructions say never to run it yourself. The fix-check command already runs it.
